hero.headline: Stuart woman arrested after deputies rescue 80 cats from home in worst hoarding case Martin County sheriff has seen
hero.body:
Martin County deputies rescued dozens of cats Monday from a Stuart home that Sheriff John Budensiek described as the worst animal hoarding case he has seen in the county. The Martin County Sheriff's Office, Animal Control and Martin County Fire Rescue responded to a home in the 11500 block of Southwest Meadowlark Circle after an investigation into reports that a U.S. Postal Service employee had been collecting feral cats along her mail route.

Budensiek identified the homeowner as 77-year-old Gail Giustino. Investigators believe she was not stealing pets but was gathering feral cats and bringing them home. Authorities obtained a search warrant after Giustino allegedly refused to allow Animal Control officers inside the home during multiple attempts over the past week. When deputies entered the house Monday, they found what the sheriff described as horrific living conditions. The home had no working air conditioning, little to no ventilation and, in some areas, up to a foot of animal feces covering the floor. Budensiek said the odor was overwhelming, and Martin County Fire Rescue's Hazardous Materials Team had to ventilate the home before rescuers could safely enter.

Giustino told deputies she believed there were at least 70 cats inside the home, all kept in cages. Authorities believe there could ultimately be 70 to 80 animals or more, including several dogs, though an exact count had not been completed Monday evening. The rescued animals are being taken to the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast, which is expected to rely on foster families and volunteers to help care for them. Authorities said they are still evaluating the animals' medical conditions.

Budensiek said Giustino was arrested on two misdemeanor animal cruelty-related charges, though investigators said they could have pursued significantly more charges. The sheriff said the criminal charges were filed primarily to obtain the search warrant, remove the animals from the home and prevent Giustino from acquiring additional animals while she seeks help through the mental health court system. Budensiek said investigators believe Giustino had good intentions despite the outcome. Officials said Animal Control had previously cited Giustino dozens of times for animal-related violations about 10 years ago, but they believe she gradually returned to hoarding animals after complying with earlier code enforcement requirements.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie shooting stemmed from jealousy over woman, police chief says
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie police now say jealousy over a woman prompted the exchange of gunfire that killed two Fort Pierce men early Sunday morning on Southeast Rivergreen Circle.
cards.body:
Police Chief Leo Niemczyk said a woman contacted Carl Loubeau, 24, whom she was dating, for a key because she was locked out of her home. When Loubeau arrived, he found her present with other people, including two males. Niemczyk said the motive behind the initial attack was jealousy over the female. The double fatal shooting occurred at about 3:30 a.m. Sunday in the 1300 block of Southeast Rivergreen Circle. When officers arrived, they found two men with multiple gunshot wounds in the driveways of a residence. Both victims, Loubeau and Juliun Stokes, 22, both from Fort Pierce, were taken to separate local hospitals, where they later died from their injuries.

Police said Loubeau was the primary aggressor in the dispute, with Dwayne Walker, 20, discharging his firearm in self-defense. Niemczyk said police think Loubeau mistook Stokes for Walker and started firing on him. Walker was in close proximity and withdrew his firearm, which is lawfully carried, and started firing on Loubeau. Police said Walker was not injured in the incident. Niemczyk said their current investigation shows that Loubeau fired eight rounds from a 9 mm pistol and one round from a .380 pistol, with Walker firing eight rounds from his .40 caliber pistol. No arrests have been made in the case.

cards.headline: Federal judge weighs Florida's assurances that Alligator Alcatraz detention facility won't reopen
cards.body:
A federal judge in Florida heard arguments Monday on whether the state can guarantee that the controversial Alligator Alcatraz immigration detention facility will remain closed. Aerial photos filed in court Monday show the remote Everglades airstrip where the facility operated for nearly a year is now empty, with the sprawling complex of trailers, tents, generators, and lights completely dismantled. Florida Division of Emergency Management officials submitted sworn declarations that the images were captured over the weekend. Nicholas Meros, an attorney representing Florida, pointed to the photos as clear evidence during the status conference, saying there is no reasonable likelihood the facility will reopen.

Immigration attorneys and former detainees sued the state and federal government, arguing their civil rights were violated because of inadequate attorney-client access at the facility. The state and federal government now contend the case is moot because the facility is closed. However, Amy Godshall, an ACLU attorney representing the plaintiffs, argued the photos and declarations provide insufficient assurance that immigrant detainees will not return to the Everglades. Godshall noted the state set up the facility in 10 days when it first opened and still controls the land, which has not been returned to Miami-Dade County. The Miami-Dade Mayor's Office confirmed Monday afternoon it has not received the land back. Godshall also pointed to what she called a lack of transparency regarding the circumstances under which the facility closed.

The facility's closure came amid reports that the state had spent more than $1 billion on operations and has not been reimbursed by the federal government. Governor Ron DeSantis announced in October that FEMA had approved a $608 million grant for Alligator Alcatraz, but court filings in a separate federal lawsuit revealed FEMA had not disbursed the funding because of ongoing litigation. FEMA has not answered direct questions about whether it would reimburse the Florida Division of Emergency Management. An ICE spokesperson told WPTV on Monday that the agency is pursuing all available options to expand bed space capacity, including partnering with states, local governments, and private sector partners.

Meros denied in court Monday that the facility closed for financial reasons or to avoid discovery in court proceedings. The state used emergency powers to take the land for Alligator Alcatraz from Miami-Dade County. While DeSantis announced in June that the facility was relocating detainees for hurricane season, he also made public statements that the facility had served its intended purpose of adding bed space for immigration detainees. Meros said he could not speak for future administrations but stated the state has no intention to reopen the facility.

cards.headline: More Than 70 Animals Found in Stuart Home During Large-Scale Hoarding Response
cards.teaser: More than 70 animals were believed to be living inside a sweltering and heavily contaminated Stuart home where Martin County authorities carried out a search warrant Monday, accord
cards.body:
More than 70 animals were believed to be living inside a sweltering and heavily contaminated Stuart home where Martin County authorities carried out a search warrant Monday, according to Sheriff John Budensiek.

Budensiek said the number of animals could ultimately reach 80 or more as deputies, Animal Services officers, Martin County Fire Rescue personnel and the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast continued working at the property.

The investigation began several weeks ago after a U.S. Postal Service employee reported that a woman appeared to be collecting or taking cats while traveling along her route, Budensiek said.

Investigators determined that the 77-year-old resident had a previous history with Martin County Animal Services. Budensiek said authorities had responded to animal-related concerns at the property approximately a decade earlier, issuing dozens of citations and helping the resident address problems involving ventilation and the care of the animals.

Animal Services officers returned to the home last week to determine whether the animals were being properly housed and whether neglect or abuse was occurring. However, Budensiek said the resident would not allow officers to fully inspect the property.

Although she surrendered several animals, she continued preventing authorities from accessing the home, according to the sheriff. Investigators subsequently obtained a search warrant and returned Monday.

Budensiek said the odor coming from the home could be detected from outside. Once responders entered, they encountered extreme heat, poor ventilation, animal waste and no functioning air conditioning.

"There could be north of 70 or 80 animals," Budensiek said during the briefing, describing areas of the home as being covered with animal feces.

The conditions were so severe that responders used protective equipment while entering and removing animals from the property. Budensiek described the interior as stifling and said crews worked to ventilate the home while attempting to safely locate and recover the animals.

Despite the conditions, Budensiek emphasized that investigators did not believe the resident was deliberately trying to harm the animals.

He said that if authorities viewed her as an intentional animal abuser, she would have been taken to jail. Instead, the sheriff characterized the situation as an animal-hoarding case involving a woman who had become overwhelmed and also needed assistance.

Budensiek said the immediate priorities were saving the animals, providing any medical treatment they require and connecting the resident with appropriate help.

The large number of animals created a significant logistical challenge for the agencies at the scene. The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast was expected to receive animals initially, but additional assistance from volunteers, rescue organizations, foster homes and potential adopters could be needed.

Each animal must also be documented and evaluated before authorities can determine its condition and appropriate placement.

Budensiek said the final number of animals remained uncertain while the operation continued. Authorities were also working through legal questions involving ownership and whether the resident would voluntarily surrender the animals.

No arrest was announced during the sheriff's briefing. Any potential citations or other legal action will depend on the results of the investigation and the conditions documented inside the home.

The response was expected to continue as crews worked through the property and arranged shelter and care for the animals.

cards.headline: Tuition-free tech charter school to open in Fort Pierce in August
cards.body:
A new tuition-free career and technical charter school is preparing to open in Fort Pierce in August, bringing a hands-on approach to education to the Treasure Coast. SouthTech Treasure Coast will give middle and high school students the opportunity to earn industry certifications while completing their traditional coursework, helping them build real-world skills and prepare for high-demand careers before they graduate. The approach mirrors what SouthTech Academy in Boynton Beach has been doing for years, combining traditional academics with hands-on career training that allows students to earn industry certifications while still in middle and high school.

The St. Lucie County School Board approved the charter application for the Fort Pierce campus in April. School leaders say they selected the Treasure Coast because of the area's growing demand for skilled workers. Carla Lovett, Executive Director of SouthTech Schools, said all students work on academics while also participating in career academies where they can earn adult level industry certifications while still in high school. Nicole Handy, Director of Expansion of SouthTech Schools, said the school is targeting high paying careers that are growing and expanding in the Fort Pierce area.

The Fort Pierce campus will serve students in grades 6 through 12, with plans to enroll about 460 students in its first year. Students will have the opportunity to choose from career academies including medical science, culinary arts, cosmetology, agriculture technology, and more. These programs are similar to those offered at the Boynton Beach campus. Meghan Hess Shamdasani, Career and Technical Education Program Coordinator, emphasized the financial benefit of the approach, saying it's better to learn something for free when you're a kid than to pay for it in college and learn. School leaders say the goal is to give students a head start on their careers by helping them graduate with valuable skills and certifications before entering the workforce or continuing their education.

SouthTech Treasure Coast will host a grand opening celebration on Saturday, July 25, from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m., giving families and community members a chance to tour the new campus and learn more about the programs being offered. The school is located at 2810 S. US Highway 1 Fort Pierce, FL 34982.

cards.headline: Family files wrongful death lawsuit against Port St. Lucie Urban Air after girl's go-kart death
cards.teaser: The parents of Emma Riddle, 6, filed a wrongful death lawsuit Monday against Urban Air Trampoline and Adventure Park after the child died in a go-kart crash at the facility in December 2025.
cards.body:
Emma Riddle, 6, visited Urban Air Trampoline and Adventure Park in Port St. Lucie in December 2025 with her mother and sister, where they rode electric go-karts. The child was seated with her mom in a double-seat go-kart while her older sister was in a single-rider go-kart. According to the family's attorney, Morgan & Morgan injury law firm, the complaint outlines multiple alleged safety protocols ignored that allegedly led Emma's go-kart to accelerate to a high speed and crash into the track wall. Emma suffered severe injuries and was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital, where she later died. A wrongful death lawsuit was filed Monday against the Port St. Lucie business, with the child's parents alleging that Urban Air created dangerous conditions that contributed to Emma's death.

Earlier this year, the Florida Department of Agriculture reached a $300,000 settlement agreement with Urban Air Adventure Park following an investigation into the fatal incident. The lawsuit alleges that at 50 inches, Emma was nearly a foot shorter and twelve years younger than the manufacturer's minimum stated recommendations for operating a double-seat go-kart, and yet she was permitted to ride. Morgan & Morgan founder John Morgan said in a statement that Urban Air has a duty to protect every child that walks through their doors, and alleged that they failed Emma in the most devastating way imaginable.

cards.headline: Childcare costs in Florida exceed affordability benchmark for 85% of families, Federal Reserve reports
cards.teaser: The Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta reports that 85.4% of Florida families spend more than the federal affordability benchmark on childcare, with median costs reaching nearly 17% of household income.
cards.body:
The cost of childcare in Florida far exceeds the affordability benchmark established by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, according to a report from the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta. The study found that 85.4% of Florida families are estimated to spend more than 7% of their income on childcare. In Florida, the median percentage of income families would need to pay for childcare is 16.8%. The estimated weekly costs for the care of infants and toddlers in Florida are $268, while preschool-aged children cost $208 per week.

From 2020 to 2024, childcare prices increased by 29%, compared with a 22% rise in overall prices, according to the Federal Reserve. The report said childcare costs now often "far exceed" the 7% of income affordability benchmark. The Atlanta Fed examined childcare costs in two states, Georgia and Florida. The study says the costs are putting significant financial pressure on parents and forcing difficult decisions on work hours and even leaving jobs.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County residents adjust diets as E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks spread
cards.teaser: Health officials confirmed five local cases of cyclospora since May, including two in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County, prompting residents to change what they eat and avoid.
cards.body:
Concerns over contaminated produce linked to E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks are prompting South Florida residents to reconsider their food choices, with some avoiding leafy greens entirely. The outbreaks have affected thousands nationwide and include lettuce connected to Taco Bell locations. Health officials have confirmed local cases stretching from the Palm Beaches to the Treasure Coast, including two cases in St. Lucie County.

 The Florida Department of Health reported five confirmed local cases of cyclospora since May. Two cases were reported in Palm Beach County, two in St. Lucie County, and one in Martin County. The contamination concerns have led families across the region to change their eating habits at restaurants, grocery stores, and fast-food chains.

 Dakota and Brynlee Rhodes, who were visiting Delray Beach with their mother Jenny, said they are trying to stay away from lettuce and stuff like that. Other families are similarly steering clear of leafy greens altogether as reports of contaminated produce continue to spread across the country. The widespread nature of the outbreaks has left many consumers uncertain about which products are safe to purchase and consume.

 Samantha Barone, a dietitian for the bariatric program at Delray Medical Center, offered guidance for consumers looking to maintain healthy diets while avoiding potentially contaminated produce. Barone recommends sticking to melon and things that have a harder skin that you can peel. She advises consumers to focus on produce with protective outer layers and to wash all fruits and vegetables thoroughly before eating them.

 For those seeking alternatives to leafy greens, Barone suggests that beans and nuts are safe options that still provide fiber and protein. She specifically recommends cleaning produce using a mixture of one part distilled white vinegar to three parts water. The outbreaks have highlighted the importance of proper food handling and preparation practices for consumers across South Florida.

cards.headline: Safe Kids Treasure Coast offering free pool alarms to Martin County residents
cards.teaser: The Florida Department of Health and Safe Kids Treasure Coast are providing a limited supply of free pool alarms to qualifying Martin County residents with residential pools.
cards.body:
The Florida Department of Health and Safe Kids Treasure Coast are providing a limited supply of free pool alarms to qualifying Martin County residents with residential pools.

 The program offers one alarm per household and has no income or priority group requirements, making it available to any qualifying resident regardless of financial status. The alarms are available while supplies last on a first-come, first-served basis, so interested residents should act promptly to secure one. Safe Kids Treasure Coast is asking residents to fill out an online survey to determine their eligibility for the program. For more information about the free pool alarm program, residents can call (772) 462-3501.

 According to the coalition, a pool alarm serves as one layer of protection and should always be used alongside close adult supervision, pool barriers and water safety education to help prevent drowning. The program emphasizes that pool alarms are not a standalone safety solution but rather part of a comprehensive approach to water safety. Residents should note that a 9-volt battery is required to operate the alarm, but the battery is not included with the free alarm.

 The initiative aims to increase water safety awareness and provide practical tools to help prevent drowning incidents in residential pools throughout Martin County. By distributing these alarms at no cost, the program seeks to remove financial barriers that might otherwise prevent families from implementing additional safety measures around their pools. The combination of free access and the comprehensive safety messaging demonstrates the coalition's commitment to protecting children and preventing water-related accidents in the community.

cards.headline: Murray Middle School demolition underway after Hurricane Milton tornado damage
cards.teaser: Demolition is underway at Murray Middle School in Martin County, marking the start of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage caused by Hurricane Milton. The project
cards.body:
Demolition is underway at Murray Middle School in Martin County, marking the start of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage caused by Hurricane Milton. The project includes reconstruction of buildings destroyed in the tornadoes, along with a new administration building, media center, art lab, and a full overhaul of the parking lot. The demolition phase alone costs $3.3 million, though the total project cost has not been finalized.

 The project is being funded by local capital improvement, sales tax and Public Education Capital Outlay. Students who were displaced from the affected classrooms will continue learning in portable classrooms until construction is complete.

 Kirstie Gernaine, coordinator of public information and community relations for the Martin County School District, said the school was already scheduled for significant construction before the hurricane struck. "Murray Middle School was already slated to get all of this construction work with a new admin area, a new media center and a brand new art lab," said Gernaine.

 "With Hurricane Milton and those tornadoes destroying the buildings in the back buildings 18, 10, and nine we were able to add these on." The school district said parents can be assured their students will be safe during construction. Barriers have already been placed around the work zone to keep students out. The district hopes to complete the renovations by December 2027.

cards.headline: Boynton Beach firefighters rescue dog from raw sewage lift station
cards.teaser: A dog fell roughly 10 to 12 feet into a lift station holding about 2 feet of raw sewage Thursday, prompting a specialized confined space rescue.
cards.body:
A dog fell roughly 10 to 12 feet into a lift station holding about 2 feet of raw sewage Thursday, prompting a specialized confined space rescue by Boynton Beach Fire Rescue Department. Squad 6 crews arrived and assessed the scene before upgrading the incident to a Special Operations confined space rescue, the department said. Firefighters developed a rescue plan and had Firefighter Ramirez properly rigged and ready to enter the lift station.

 From the time he went on air, Firefighter Ramirez rescued the dog and safely exited the lift station in just 4 minutes, the department said. Once above ground, crews decontaminated the dog and gave it oxygen before turning it over to Animal Control. Animal Control successfully reunited the dog with its owner, according to a Facebook post from the department.

cards.headline: Wellington teen injured after electric bike rider strikes him during stunt near Lion Country Safari
cards.teaser: A Wellington teenager suffered multiple injuries, including broken bones, after being struck by an electric bike rider performing a wheelie on Tuesday night.
cards.body:
Seventeen-year-old Chad Filer said he was riding his scooter along a relatively isolated stretch of road between the Deer Run community and Lion Country Safari on Tuesday night when three teenage boys on dirt and electric bikes approached him. According to Chad, one rider began performing a wheelie and intentionally swerved toward him in what he described as a common "bike life" stunt meant to intimidate people before pulling away at the last second, but instead the bike struck the right side of his body.

 Chad estimates the rider was traveling around 40 mph when the impact sent him to the ground. A driver stopped to help, and Chad said the riders initially stayed nearby and told him he was "fine," but once witnesses called 911, the group fled.

 Doctors found Chad suffered broken metatarsal bones, three broken toes, significant bruising and multiple road rash injuries across his chest, knee, elbow and side. His mother, Cortez Hornsby, said part of one nipple was partially detached in the crash. The family faces mounting medical expenses because Chad's health insurance through work was not scheduled to begin until next month.

 Hornsby says she called the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office and was told this is a county-wide problem. She also says deputies told her that based on how isolated the crash site is and the lack of cameras, it may be difficult to find the teens. Chad cannot work while he heals, and the scooter he relied on for transportation was heavily damaged.

hero.headline: 2 men killed in early morning shooting in Port St. Lucie neighborhood
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie Police Department is investigating a double fatal shooting that occurred early Sunday morning in a residential neighborhood. Officers responded around 3:30 a.m. to the 1300 block of Southeast Rivergreen Circle after receiving multiple 911 calls reporting gunshots.

When officers arrived, they found two adult men suffering from multiple gunshot wounds in the driveways of a residence. Both victims were taken to separate local hospitals, where they later died from their injuries. Police identified the victims as Carl Loubeau, 24, and Juliun Stokes, 22. Preliminary investigators believe some of the people involved had been socializing earlier in the evening before returning to a home on Southeast Rivergreen Circle. Police said a verbal altercation occurred outside the residence over a residential key and escalated into an exchange of gunfire between two of the individuals involved.

Neighbor John Adams was working on his bicycle in his garage when he heard the gunfire. "I was just working on my bicycle and I heard gunshots. Maybe two, three and I stayed in the garage and then I heard a girl screaming," Adams said. "Every police officer in Port St. Lucie was here, there was twenty squads, two ambulances, two firetrucks, a helicopter. It was just mayhem." Adams said a police officer told him they took a picture of 16 casings. "Just devastating, terrible. My heart goes out to them," he said. Another neighbor who did not want to be identified said she dialed 911 and stayed with one of the wounded men until help arrived.

Investigators believe the shooting was an isolated incident involving people who knew one another and said there is no ongoing threat to the public. All parties involved have either been detained or are cooperating with investigators, according to police. The investigation remains active as detectives continue conducting interviews, processing evidence and reviewing available information. Police said additional details, including any potential criminal charges, will be released as the investigation progresses. Anyone with information who has not yet spoken with detectives is asked to contact the Port St. Lucie Police Department.

cards.headline: Firefighters union disputes St. Lucie County Fire District hazing findings, calls terminations unjust
cards.teaser: Professional Firefighters and Paramedics of St. Lucie County is pushing back against the fire district's decision to terminate three firefighters and suspend two others for incidents that occurred in March and September 2024.
cards.body:
Local 1377 President Ryan Sapp stated in a letter obtained by WPTV that the incidents did not involve any hazing. Sapp pointed to the Fort Pierce Police Department's report, which he said described the situation, in part, as "found coworkers entertaining each other." Professional Firefighters and Paramedics of St. Lucie County, IAFF Local 1377, said the St. Lucie County Fire District wrongly terminated and suspended the five members for their involvement in incidents that occurred in March and September 2024. Local 1377 has demanded arbitration for all five members. The union's position is that all five were wrongly found to be in violation of fire district policies and disciplined without just cause. Sapp also noted that members involved in the incidents were treated differently during the investigative and disciplinary processes, with some receiving no discipline at all.

The union raised concerns about the outside law firm the fire district hired to conduct its investigation, Allen, Norton & Blue. Local 1377 and its legal counsel said the investigation was not conducted in an impartial or unbiased manner. "The nature of the questions asked, as well as the way in which they were asked or not asked, reflects a predetermined conclusion rather than an objective fact-finding process," Sapp stated in the letter. Sapp noted that the same firm that conducted the investigation has since been hired by the fire district to represent it at arbitration. The union said it has made every effort to resolve the matters through the grievance procedures outlined in its collective bargaining agreement and remains willing to negotiate a resolution that would avoid the costs of arbitration. Sapp said Fire Chief Jeff Lee has not offered any concessions or proposed resolutions. According to the district, administrators first received videos in March 2026 showing what they described as senior firefighters using a modified bug zapper to administer electric shocks to probationary and apprentice firefighters while on duty.

Officials said Animal Control had previously cited Giustino dozens of times for animal-related violations about 10 years ago.

cards.headline: Two men killed in early morning shooting on Southeast Rivergreen Circle in Port St. Lucie
cards.teaser: Carl Loubeau, 24, and Juliun Stokes, 22, died Sunday morning after a dispute over a residential key escalated into gunfire.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie police responded around 3:30 a.m. Sunday to the 1300 block of Southeast Rivergreen Circle after receiving multiple 911 calls reporting gunshots.

 When officers arrived, they found two adult men suffering from multiple gunshot wounds in the driveways of a residence. Both victims were taken to separate local hospitals, where they later died from their injuries. Police identified the victims as Carl Loubeau, 24, and Juliun Stokes, 22.

 Preliminary investigators believe some of the people involved had been socializing earlier in the evening before returning to a home on Southeast Rivergreen Circle. Police said a verbal altercation occurred outside the residence over a residential key and escalated into an exchange of gunfire between two of the individuals involved. The investigation remains active as detectives continue conducting interviews, processing evidence and reviewing available information. Police said additional details, including any potential criminal charges, will be released as the investigation progresses.

 Neighbor John Adams told WPTV reporter Zitlali Solache he was awake working in his garage when the shooting occurred. "I was just working on my bicycle and I heard gunshots. Maybe two, three and I stayed in the garage and then I heard a girl screaming," Adams said.

 He described a massive emergency response to the scene. "Every police officer in Port St. Lucie was here, there was twenty squads, two ambulances, two firetrucks, a helicopter.

 It was just mayhem," Adams said. He added that a police officer told him they took a picture of 16 casings. "Just devastating, terrible.

 My heart goes out to them," Adams said. Another neighbor who did not want to be identified told WPTV she dialed 911 and stayed with one of the wounded men until help arrived.

 Investigators believe the shooting was an isolated incident involving people who knew one another and said there is no ongoing threat to the public. All parties involved have either been detained or are cooperating with investigators, according to police. Anyone with information who has not yet spoken with detectives is asked to contact the Port St. Lucie Police Department.

cards.headline: Family files wrongful death lawsuit after 6-year-old dies at Urban Air Adventure Park in Port St. Lucie
cards.teaser: A wrongful death lawsuit has been filed against Urban Air Trampoline and Adventure Park in Port St. Lucie after 6-year-old Emma Riddle died from injuries sustained on a go-kart rid
cards.body:
A wrongful death lawsuit has been filed against Urban Air Trampoline and Adventure Park in Port St. Lucie after 6-year-old Emma Riddle died from injuries sustained on a go-kart ride in December 2025. The child's parents allege that Urban Air created the dangerous conditions that contributed to Emma's death. Emma visited the adventure park with her mother and sister, where they went on the electric go-karts ride.

 The child was seated with her mom in a double-seat go-kart while her older sister was in a single-rider go-kart. According to the family's attorney, Morgan & Morgan injury law firm, multiple alleged safety protocols were ignored that allegedly led Emma's go-kart to accelerate to a high speed and crash into the track wall. Emma suffered severe injuries and was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital, where she later died.

 The child's family claims the adventure park ignored safety rules and manufacturer guidelines. At 50 inches, Emma was nearly a foot shorter and twelve years younger than the manufacturer's minimum stated recommendations for operating a double-seat go-kart, and yet she was permitted to ride, the lawsuit alleges. Earlier this year, documents showed the Florida Department of Agriculture reached a $300,000 settlement agreement with Urban Air Adventure Park following an investigation into the fatal incident.

 Morgan & Morgan founder John Morgan said in a statement that Emma Riddle was a bright, beautiful 6-year-old girl whose life was tragically cut short. What was meant to be a joyful family outing became every family's worst nightmare, Morgan said. Urban Air has a duty to protect every child that walks through their doors, and the firm alleges that they failed Emma in the most devastating way imaginable. Morgan said the firm will stop at nothing to hold Urban Air accountable for this tragedy and make sure no other family has to endure this kind of loss.

 WPTV has reached out to Urban Air for a response to the lawsuit. The wrongful death case centers on allegations that the adventure park allowed Emma to ride despite her not meeting the manufacturer's safety requirements for height and age. The lawsuit claims that Urban Air's failure to follow proper safety protocols and guidelines directly contributed to the fatal accident that took the young girl's life during what should have been a fun family outing.

hero.headline: JetBlue cancels Vero Beach to JFK flights in September, cites low demand
hero.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast. Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said JetBlue was not seeing the ridership numbers it had hoped for on the JFK route. The decision reflects how the airline industry operates, with air carriers fluctuating based on demand.

All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds. JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service. Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information.

Not everyone agrees the route had a fair shot. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time. "I think if they hung in there, it would have worked. I think it would have built up pretty good," Ahern said. He emphasized the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach. "It's easy. It's close," Ahern said.

Dambeck said the Boston route is performing well and seeing great demand. Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time. As for whether the JFK route could return in the future, Dambeck said the door is not closed. "They'll evaluate continuously. So just because it's gone now doesn't mean that it never will come back," Dambeck said. The decision reflects how the airline industry operates. "It's just the way that that market works, and air carriers will fluctuate based off of demand," Dambeck said.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County woman wins $5 million from scratch-off ticket bought in Fort Pierce
cards.teaser: Maria Duran, 57, claimed a $5 million top prize from a scratch-off game she purchased at a Fort Pierce store.
cards.body: Florida Lottery officials announced Friday that Maria Duran, 57, of St. Lucie County claimed a $5 million top prize from the $5,000,000 CROSSWORD CASH scratch-off game on April 6, turning $20 into $5 million. Duran chose to receive her winnings as a one-time, lump-sum payment of $3,262,138. She purchased her winning ticket from PK 2 Quick Mart, located at 4101 Okeechobee Road in Fort Pierce. The game's overall odds of winning are 1-in-2.90, but the chance of winning $5 million playing this game is 1-in-4,018,135.
