cards.headline: E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks hit Treasure Coast, residents avoid lettuce and berries
cards.teaser: Two confirmed cases of cyclospora infections occurred in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County since May, part of nationwide E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks linked to contamin
cards.body:
Two confirmed cases of cyclospora infections occurred in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County since May, part of nationwide E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks linked to contaminated lettuce, according to the Florida Department of Health. Palm Beach County reported two additional cases. Thousands across the United States have been affected by the outbreaks, including lettuce connected to Taco Bell locations.

 Residents across South Florida are changing their diets in response to the health threat. Dakota and Brynlee Rhodes, visiting Delray Beach with their mother Jenny, said they are staying away from lettuce. Jenny Rhodes said she misses salads and berries but prefers being careful.

 George Lorenz said he heard about the outbreak and is avoiding contaminated foods while eating pizza in downtown West Palm Beach on Clematis Street with his father Brian. Hendriette Peckens in Boynton Beach bought two big bags of oranges, bread and apples instead of produce and planned to cook Alaskan salmon for dinner.

 Samantha Barone, a dietitian for the bariatric program at Delray Medical Center, said consumers should focus on produce with protective outer layers like melons, bananas and avocados. She said people should stick to melon and things with harder skin that can be peeled, but emphasized the importance of washing them before cutting and peeling. Barone recommended washing all fruits and vegetables thoroughly before eating them and said beans and nuts are safe alternatives that provide fiber and protein.

 She warned against bagged lettuce and recommended buying whole heads of lettuce and peeling away the outer layers. She also advised avoiding berries, especially raspberries, because they are difficult to clean properly. Brian Lorenz said he is not avoiding anything but is washing all food.

 Barone recommended cleaning produce using a one to three part mixture of distilled white vinegar and water, then soaking, massaging and cleaning off produce before cooking vegetables. The outbreaks stem from contaminated produce that can cause severe stomach illness and intense diarrhea. Barone emphasized that the outbreaks are not an excuse to abandon healthy eating, telling people not to say to heck with fruits and vegetables and hit the donuts. She said consumers still want to remain healthy despite the contamination concerns affecting produce typically considered healthier options.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce neighbors pack planning meeting over Causeway Cove high-rise development proposal
cards.teaser: The Causeway Cove development project was reviewed by the Fort Pierce Planning Board on Monday. The project includes five high-rise buildings, including a 17-story building standing 192 feet tall.
cards.body:
The Causeway Cove development project was reviewed by the Fort Pierce Planning Board on Monday. The project, located off Seaway Drive, includes five high-rise buildings, including a 17-story building standing 192 feet tall, more than four times the city's height limit. Plans also call for two hotels and more than 70,000 square feet of retail space.

 The development qualifies under the Live Local Act, a state law passed in 2023 that allows developers to bypass height and density restrictions as long as they set aside 40% of units for affordable housing for at least 30 years. The project includes more than 900 apartments and condos, with 365 of those designated as affordable housing.

 Neighbors packed the chamber during the Monday meeting. Buster Brewster, a boater at Causeway Cove Marina, said he worries the project will change the character of the area. Dennis Fein raised concerns about traffic, saying nobody has thought this out and predicting massive traffic jams with nobody able to get on or off the island.

 City Planning Director Kev Freeman said developers must add traffic mitigation efforts and any required intersection or access improvements. City Commissioner Michael Broderick said the city has no authority over whether the project is approved, stating the city does not have a play here and this is regulated by the state of Florida in the entirety. City commissioners are scheduled to hear a review of the project as the next step in the process.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie couple fights rezoning of lot behind home near Crosstown Parkway
cards.teaser: A Port St. Lucie couple is searching for answers after the city council voted to rezone the lot behind their home from residential to commercial.
cards.body:
Joseph and Margaret Mucciolo have called Port St. Lucie home since purchasing their property, drawn by what Margaret described as the beautiful setting and backyard views of nature. In a unanimous vote, the Port St.

 Lucie City Council approved rezoning the lot behind their yard, where trees currently stand, from residential to commercial. One council member said the change is necessary to reduce traffic in the neighborhood, explaining that adding commercial closer to neighborhoods reduces the length of trips, which reduces overall traffic because shorter trips reduce the burden on the overall network.

 The Mucciolos fought the rezoning for months and feel their voices have gone unheard. The council held its second reading Monday. While there was public comment, it was what is called a quasi-judicial hearing, meaning council members act as a panel of judges, applying existing zoning rules to a specific property and making decisions based strictly on sworn testimony and factual evidence, not public opinion.

 The Mucciolos say the process needs to change to be logical, transparent, caring, and provide hope for people. They say they will be exploring any kind of appeal process to change this outcome or to change the next one. Joseph Mucciolo said he believes in six months or a year, the trees behind their home will be gone.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound couple seeks support as husband battles head and neck cancer
cards.teaser: Dave and Faren Motz of Hobe Sound are asking for community support as Dave battles head and neck cancer, facing nearly $20,000 in out-of-pocket costs for treatment.
cards.body:
A Hobe Sound couple is asking for community support as they navigate a cancer diagnosis. Dave and Faren Motz met in South Florida before moving to Maui, where they married and raised their family. Faren homeschooled all three of their children, and the family started a farm where they served children. Years later, the couple moved to Hobe Sound and purchased a property, but just months after settling in, Dave was diagnosed with head and neck cancer.

 As the couple searched for healthcare in Florida, AdventHealth in Celebration provided programs and grants that became a critical resource. Dave underwent nearly seven weeks of daily radiation treatments. The repeated visits to Orlando, biopsies, scans, and exams added up, costing the couple nearly $20,000 out of pocket.

 Their age and income kept them from qualifying for Medicare or Medicaid. Dave, a former firefighter who had long been the family's provider, now has an 85% chance of recovery according to doctors. Faren now works to support them both at Latitudes at the Jupiter Beach Resort, where those who want to show support can visit. Those who would like to contribute financially can donate to the family's GoFundMe at Standing with Dave Motz in his cancer battle.

hero.headline: Messi bathed Yamal as baby in 2007 photo shoot, now they meet in World Cup final
hero.teaser: A 2007 charity calendar photo shoot paired teenage Lionel Messi with infant Lamine Yamal. Now 19 years later, they face off in Sunday's World Cup final.
hero.body:
Photographer Joan Monfort took photos in 2007 of a teenage Lionel Messi bathing infant Lamine Yamal in a plastic bathtub as part of a charity calendar produced by local newspaper Sport and UNICEF. Monfort, who works as a freelance photojournalist for The Associated Press, took the photos after Yamal's mother won a raffle of families in the city of Mataró near Barcelona who wanted to participate.

 Soccer destiny paired her baby boy with the Argentine who would become the greatest of all time. Messi left Barcelona in 2021 when the club was in financial trouble. Yamal erupted at the club two years later.

 Monfort had no recollection of the photos until Yamal's father posted one on social media during the 2024 European Championship, when a teenage Yamal led Spain to the title. The photo went viral then, but interest has skyrocketed with Sunday's World Cup final between Argentina and Spain approaching. Monfort said he has been bombarded by queries for the photos by professional media outlets while also seeing his images reproduced countless times on social media and the internet without any credit or compensation.

 The 19-year-old Yamal will face a Messi who is 20 years his senior in Sunday's final. Monfort, 58, is considering traveling to see the final in New Jersey. He said his heart is split and he does not know if he wants Messi or Yamal to win.

cards.headline: President Trump to Attend World Cup Final in New Jersey with Stepped-Up Security
cards.teaser: The World Cup final Sunday in New Jersey has been designated a Level 1 Special Event with President Trump attending the trophy presentation and enhanced security from multiple federal agencies.
cards.body:
The 2026 FIFA World Cup began with 48 teams playing over 39 days. Now it comes down to one final match Sunday in New Jersey. As Argentina and Spain prepare to take the pitch, a sprawling network of federal agents, local law enforcement, and private companies continue with a game plan two years in the making to ensure the final is safe.

 A joint operations center in New York has helped oversee security and monitor threats in host cities throughout the tournament, with thousands of personnel on the ground and a team with an eye on the skies. The FBI has seized hundreds of drones flying in restricted airspace near stadiums during the tournament.

 The final will include a beefed-up Secret Service perimeter, with President Trump attending the trophy presentation. White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt says his attendance will cap what has been the most watched, most secure, and most successful World Cup in American history. When Trump attended an NBA Finals game last month in New York, police shut down several city blocks around the arena and fans were forced to wait in extra-long lines to go through enhanced security.

 The World Cup final is a Level 1 Special Event, the highest possible security designation, with added resources from the Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Defense, and the FBI. No one will be allowed to simply walk up to the stadium or drive a personal vehicle.

cards.headline: Major League Baseball Restricts iPad Use in Dugouts to Block AI Decision-Making
cards.teaser: MLB has made custom tabs on dugout iPads inaccessible starting Wednesday to prevent teams from using artificial intelligence to make in-game decisions about substitutions and pitch calling.
cards.body:
Major League Baseball is restricting iPad usage in dugouts to prevent the tablets from running artificial intelligence to help make decisions. The tablets have access to video and league-provided data, and also included a custom tab where teams could access other programs. MLB made the custom tabs inaccessible to teams starting Wednesday night, when the second half of the season started.

 MLB executive vice president of baseball operations Morgan Sword wrote in a June 11 memo to general managers, assistant GMs and video coordinators that in many cases, the custom tab had expanded the use of the dugout iPads beyond their originally intended purpose to include recommendations regarding substitutions, pitch calling, and other in-game decisions traditionally made by players and coaches. The memo was first reported by The Athletic and was obtained by The Associated Press.

 A review by the competition committee found clubs had been compliant with the regulations. Sword wrote that instituting this prohibition beginning with the second half of the season is intended to provide clubs that have relied on the custom tab with appropriate lead-time to make any necessary adjustments. MLB started a pilot program allowing use of iPads in dugouts with restrictions late in the 2015 season and expanded their use in 2016 under a deal with Apple. Video was eliminated in the 2020 COVID season following the Houston Astros' sign-stealing scandal, then returned in 2021.

cards.headline: Britain's Josh Kerr breaks mile world record with 3:42.66 run in London
cards.teaser: Josh Kerr shattered a 27-year-old world record on Saturday, running the mile in 3:42.66 at a Diamond League event in London.
cards.body:
Great Britain's Josh Kerr ran the mile in 3:42.66 on Saturday in London, breaking Hicham El Guerrouj's previous mark of 3:43.13 set in 1999. The 27-year-old made no secret that he was targeting the long-standing record at Saturday's Diamond League event in London. Earlier this week, he revealed he ran 2:42.45 in a 1,200-meter time trial.

 His sponsor, Brooks, dubbed the effort "Project 222," referencing the number of seconds in 3 minutes, 42 seconds. American Yared Nuguse finished second in 3:45.69.

 Kerr has emerged as one of the world's top middle-distance runners, winning bronze in the 1,500 meters at the Tokyo Olympics and silver at the 2024 Paris Olympics. Before turning professional, Kerr starred at the University of New Mexico, where he won multiple NCAA titles. He also set an NCAA indoor mile record of 3:35.01 in 2018. Kerr's record-setting run came during the Diamond League, an established international circuit of professional track and field events.

cards.headline: Spain defeats Argentina 1-0 to win 2026 World Cup in extra time thriller
cards.teaser: Spain defeated Argentina 1-0 on Sunday to win the 2026 FIFA World Cup championship. Ferran Torres scored the winning goal in the 106th minute of extra time, burying a left-footed s
cards.body:
Spain defeated Argentina 1-0 on Sunday to win the 2026 FIFA World Cup championship. Ferran Torres scored the winning goal in the 106th minute of extra time, burying a left-footed shot just under the crossbar after pouncing on a bouncing ball in the box. It is Spain's second World Cup championship and first since 2010.

 Spain was absolutely dominant throughout the match in terms of possession and shot attempts. The team took 15 shots in regulation while Argentina managed none. Spain also won nine corners compared to Argentina's single corner kick.

 Despite this overwhelming advantage, Lionel Messi and Argentina found a way to hang on and force the match into extra time. Torres broke through in the opening moment of the second 15-minute period of extra time to finally secure the victory for Spain.

 Argentina's task became even more difficult when Enzo Fernandez was sent off in second-half stoppage time after receiving his second yellow card. Fernandez was carded for a reckless play that sent Spain defender Pau Cubarsi cartwheeling into the air, forcing Argentina to finish the match with only 10 players. About two minutes after play resumed, another foul gave Lamine Yamal a chance to seal the victory from about 22 yards out on a free kick.

 His curling strike toward the right post was saved by Argentina goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez, who made a diving stop for his 10th save of the afternoon, the most ever recorded in a World Cup final. Martinez leaped to his feet afterward, punching the air and encouraging the crowd to get loud before the match eventually went to extra time.

 With the victory, Spain became the first nation to simultaneously hold the World Cup crowns in both men's and women's soccer. The final was the 104th and last match of the expanded 48-team tournament played across the United States, Canada and Mexico. Because there were more matches than any previous World Cup, the tournament produced 308 total goals, more than any other edition in history. According to FIFA, the 2026 World Cup was officially the most attended ever.

cards.headline: Flip City Gym and Cheer gymnasts earn top 15 national finish, qualify for Junior Olympics
cards.teaser: Three gymnasts from Flip City Gym and Cheer secured a top 15 finish at AAU Nationals in Knoxville, Tennessee last month and qualified for the Junior Olympics in Iowa next month. Sk
cards.body:
Three gymnasts from Flip City Gym and Cheer secured a top 15 finish at AAU Nationals in Knoxville, Tennessee last month and qualified for the Junior Olympics in Iowa next month. Skylar Rose-Daris, Victoria Supan, and Charli Rine represented the gym at the national competition and will advance to compete at the higher level. The trio each discovered gymnastics through unique experiences, with Rose-Daris crediting her ability to do a cartwheel, Supan finding inspiration from watching gymnasts on YouTube, and Rine enjoying the opportunity to continuously learn new skills.

 Head Coach Candice Lazuka praised the team's performance throughout the season, noting they competed at local meets before advancing through states and regionals to reach nationals. At the AAU Nationals competition in Knoxville, the team delivered an exceptional performance that nearly achieved a perfect score. Lazuka explained that earning a perfect 10 is extremely difficult, but the gymnasts managed to score a 9.9, coming very close to perfection. The strong showing at nationals secured their qualification for the Junior Olympics.

 The three gymnasts expressed excitement about the upcoming opportunity to compete at the Junior Olympics in Iowa. Rose-Daris said it's going to be really fun that she's going to an entire different part of the world. Supan described her feelings about the achievement, saying it's happy and exciting at the same time. The young athletes are preparing to take on competitors from across the country at the prestigious event.

 Looking ahead to the Junior Olympics competition, the gymnasts are setting their goals and focusing on specific events. When asked what she is focused on heading into the Junior Olympics, Rine said getting first place on floors. The qualification represents a significant achievement for both the individual gymnasts and Flip City Gym and Cheer as a whole.

 The team's progression from local competitions through the state and regional levels to nationals, and now to the Junior Olympics, demonstrates the dedication and skill development that Lazuka has cultivated in her athletes. The upcoming competition in Iowa will provide Rose-Daris, Supan, and Rine the chance to test themselves against the nation's top junior gymnasts.

cards.headline: Giannis Antetokounmpo, Bobby Portis Jr. join Miami Heat in major trade
cards.teaser: The Miami Heat introduced two-time NBA MVP Giannis Antetokounmpo and forward Bobby Portis Jr. at the Kaseya Center on Thursday, with both players receiving standing ovations from fans.
cards.body:
Thursday afternoon, loud chants of "Giannis" filled the Kaseya Center as the Miami Heat introduced their latest acquisitions. Heat Head Coach Erik Spoelstra said Pat Riley asked him if he wanted to coach Giannis Antetokounmpo, and he said yes. The move brings a two-time MVP, NBA champion, and Finals MVP to South Florida, though questions remain about whether the Heat gave up too much for the star coming off back-to-back injury-filled seasons.

 Antetokounmpo, who stands 6'11 and weighs 240 pounds, told reporters he thrives on pressure and needs it at this point in his career to go to the next level and get out of his comfort zone. He said he was not there to talk about measurables but rather how many championships he can help bring to Miami. Antetokounmpo said he feels like whenever he puts his mind to something, he usually accomplishes it, and this is the best route for him to win more titles.

 The Heat also introduced forward Bobby Portis Jr., who said he prides himself on working every day in the summer to get better and has been coming off the bench his whole career as a sixth man type of guy. Portis said being aggressive is what he has always been about, a mindset that Riley and Spoelstra believe embodies the Miami Heat way of playing basketball.

 Portis, who has been playing with Antetokounmpo for six years, said his relationship with Bam Adebayo has been built off being competitors. Spoelstra said the squad featuring Antetokounmpo, Portis, and Adebayo will play a lot of positionless basketball. Antetokounmpo told reporters he wants to be coached hard so everyone else will follow, adding he does not want feedback sugar-coated and needs the truth so he can apply it to his game.

hero.headline: Boca Raton TLC Program Offers Summer Service Projects for South Florida Families
hero.teaser: B'nai Torah Congregation's TLC Program connects volunteers with hands-on service projects ranging from food support and shoe donations to pantry stocking and literacy efforts.
hero.body:
B'nai Torah Congregation's TLC Program is offering South Florida families a range of hands-on service projects this summer, from food support and shoe donations to pantry stocking, literacy efforts and care for seniors. Led by Summer Faerman, the program connects volunteers of all ages with mitzvah opportunities, or meaningful good deeds, as part of the congregation's broader community outreach efforts.

 The TLC Program stands for Tzedakah, Learning and Chesed, and has made service a central part of synagogue life since 2012. The program provides a way for individuals and families to put Jewish values into action while helping people in need across South Florida. It addresses multiple community concerns including hunger, homelessness, literacy, elder care, vulnerable populations and special needs. Organizers emphasize that the projects are open to everyone in the community, not only members of B'nai Torah Congregation, with the goal of making service practical, welcoming and easy to begin.

 Participants can volunteer in various ways throughout the summer. Projects include making sandwiches, serving meals, collecting and cleaning shoes, stocking Little Free Pantries, preparing backpacks for back-to-school efforts, creating Bags of Hope and helping seniors with technology. Organizers plan to demonstrate volunteer projects such as wrapping presents, making flower arrangements, preparing sandwiches, collecting shoes and assembling supplies for people in need. The variety of options allows families to choose activities that match their interests and schedules.

 As summer continues, the TLC Program offers families a way to stay connected, teach children about giving back and support neighbors throughout South Florida. B'nai Torah Congregation says the program is built around the idea that small acts of service can strengthen the larger community. More information about the TLC Program is available through B'nai Torah Congregation's website.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County Food Bank serves 2,500 hot meals daily to children at 35 summer sites
cards.teaser: The Palm Beach County Food Bank in Lake Worth Beach is serving approximately 2,500 hot meals each day to nearly 1,250 children through Florida's Summer BreakSpot program while school is out.
cards.body:
The Palm Beach County Food Bank is serving approximately 2,500 hot meals each day to nearly 1,250 children through Florida's Summer BreakSpot program, according to Food Bank leaders. The nonprofit organization supports more than 35 Summer BreakSpot sites across Palm Beach County while school is out for the summer. During a live Shining A Light broadcast on WPTV, CEO Jamie Kendall and Culinary Director Chef Doug Barg gave viewers a behind-the-scenes look inside the Michelle Hagerty Community Kitchen, where meals are prepared and loaded onto trucks for early morning deliveries across the county.

 The organization prepared more than 36,000 hot meals in June alone. According to the Palm Beach County Food Bank, hunger doesn't take a summer break, highlighting the need for continued support during the summer months. The Summer BreakSpot program provides free meals to children and teens 18 and younger during the summer when school cafeterias are closed. Food Bank leaders said the meals are distributed through partner locations across Palm Beach County to help families facing food insecurity during the summer. Kendall said the Food Bank's partnership with Summer BreakSpot helps ensure children continue receiving nutritious meals while school is out.

 During the broadcast, viewers got a close look at the large-scale kitchen operation responsible for preparing meals daily. Chef Barg walked viewers through the food production process, showing how culinary teams prepare, package and organize meals before they are loaded onto delivery trucks. The loading dock operation featured drivers and volunteers preparing for morning deliveries to Summer BreakSpot sites throughout Palm Beach County. The Palm Beach County Food Bank said volunteers and community support are critical to maintaining the program during the busy summer season.

 The Palm Beach County Food Bank is located at 701 Boutwell Road, Suite A-1, in Lake Worth Beach. Food Bank leaders said the organization continues seeking volunteers, donations and community partnerships to support its mission of reducing childhood hunger in Palm Beach County. Families looking for Summer BreakSpot meal locations can find participating sites throughout the county during the summer months.

cards.headline: Downtown Delray Beach launches Wellness Pass with free fitness classes and spa deals for July and August
cards.teaser: The Delray Beach Downtown Development Authority launched the Downtown Delray Wellness Pass for July and August. The mobile-exclusive pass allows users to access complimentary classes, discounted wellness treatments and promotions from participating businesses.
cards.body:
Downtown Delray Beach is encouraging residents and visitors to prioritize health and self-care this summer through a new Wellness Pass featuring free fitness classes, yoga sessions, spa discounts and wellness-focused offers across the city's downtown district. The Delray Beach Downtown Development Authority launched the Downtown Delray Wellness Pass for July and August.

 According to the DDA, the mobile-exclusive pass allows users to access complimentary classes, discounted wellness treatments and promotions from participating businesses throughout Downtown Delray Beach. The pass does not require an app download. Miller Physical Therapy is also participating with wellness-related services and promotions. The program arrives as wellness tourism and fitness-focused experiences continue to grow in popularity across South Florida. Many consumers are seeking affordable ways to stay active, reduce stress and support local businesses during the summer months.

cards.headline: Delray Beach dance studio hosts Bridgerton masquerade gala July 24 for ninth anniversary
cards.teaser: Fred Astaire Dance Studios Delray Beach is celebrating nine years with a Bridgerton-style masquerade gala featuring themed decor and dancing.
cards.body:
Fred Astaire Dance Studios Delray Beach, located at 247 SE Sixth Ave., is hosting a Bridgerton-style masquerade gala on July 24 to celebrate its ninth anniversary. The studio is owned by world champion dancers Mar Martinez and Clifton Sepulveda and has built a reputation for welcoming dancers of all experience levels, from beginners to competitive performers. The anniversary gala will feature themed décor, dancing and a celebration of the studio's growth over the past nine years.

 The studio is launching a Summer Boot Camp series beginning July 18 and continuing every Saturday through August. According to Fred Astaire Dance Studios Delray Beach, the classes are designed to help participants learn ballroom and Latin dance fundamentals in a fun, supportive environment. Another upcoming event is a DJ Latin Dance Night open to the public on July 31 from 8 p.m. to 10 p.m. Martinez and Sepulveda are also preparing to teach a dance class at Florida Atlantic University beginning in August. More information about upcoming events and classes is available at FredAstaireDelrayBeach.com.

cards.headline: Palm Beach Zoo extends Kids Free program through August 10
cards.teaser: Palm Beach Zoo extended its Kids Free promotion through August 10, allowing up to four children ages 3 to 12 to receive free admission with one adult ticket.
cards.body:
Palm Beach Zoo extended its popular Kids Free promotion through Aug. 10, according to zoo officials. Under the program, up to four children ages 3 to 12 receive free admission with the purchase of one adult ticket. Amanda Joiner, the zoo's chief marketing and technology officer, shared the updates during WPTV's "Shining A Light" segment from the zoo Monday morning. Joiner said the extension is designed to help local families enjoy affordable outings during the hottest stretch of summer while still supporting the zoo's conservation mission. Zoo officials emphasized that families still receive the full zoo experience through the promotion, including access to exhibits, shaded walkways and animal encounters. The zoo is also encouraging visitors to stay cool with indoor spaces, shaded pathways and frozen treats available throughout the park.

 The zoo's newest koala joey is officially a boy and now has a name: Bonza. Joiner said that's Aussie slang for "awesome" or "excellent" during the interview. Palm Beach Zoo also announced the return of its Wild Night Out series, an adults-only after-hours experience happening on the last Saturdays of July, August and September. The themed nights include "Paws & Santa Claus" in July, "Tails & Touchdowns" in August and "Decades After Dark" in September. The events will feature live entertainment, themed activities and performances from bands including Whiskey Six and Snapback. Palm Beach Zoo is located at 1301 Summit Blvd.

hero.headline: Federal judge weighs Florida's assurances that Alligator Alcatraz detention facility won't reopen
hero.body:
A federal judge in Florida heard arguments Monday on whether the state can guarantee that the controversial Alligator Alcatraz immigration detention facility will remain closed. Aerial photos filed in court Monday show the remote Everglades airstrip where the facility operated for nearly a year is now empty, with the sprawling complex of trailers, tents, generators, and lights completely dismantled. Florida Division of Emergency Management officials submitted sworn declarations that the images were captured over the weekend. Nicholas Meros, an attorney representing Florida, pointed to the photos as clear evidence during the status conference, saying there is no reasonable likelihood the facility will reopen.

Immigration attorneys and former detainees sued the state and federal government, arguing their civil rights were violated because of inadequate attorney-client access at the facility. The state and federal government now contend the case is moot because the facility is closed. However, Amy Godshall, an ACLU attorney representing the plaintiffs, argued the photos and declarations provide insufficient assurance that immigrant detainees will not return to the Everglades. Godshall noted the state set up the facility in 10 days when it first opened and still controls the land, which has not been returned to Miami-Dade County. The Miami-Dade Mayor's Office confirmed Monday afternoon it has not received the land back. Godshall also pointed to what she called a lack of transparency regarding the circumstances under which the facility closed.

The facility's closure came amid reports that the state had spent more than $1 billion on operations and has not been reimbursed by the federal government. Governor Ron DeSantis announced in October that FEMA had approved a $608 million grant for Alligator Alcatraz, but court filings in a separate federal lawsuit revealed FEMA had not disbursed the funding because of ongoing litigation. FEMA has not answered direct questions about whether it would reimburse the Florida Division of Emergency Management. An ICE spokesperson told WPTV on Monday that the agency is pursuing all available options to expand bed space capacity, including partnering with states, local governments, and private sector partners.

Meros denied in court Monday that the facility closed for financial reasons or to avoid discovery in court proceedings. The state used emergency powers to take the land for Alligator Alcatraz from Miami-Dade County. While DeSantis announced in June that the facility was relocating detainees for hurricane season, he also made public statements that the facility had served its intended purpose of adding bed space for immigration detainees. Meros said he could not speak for future administrations but stated the state has no intention to reopen the facility.

cards.headline: Childcare costs in Florida exceed affordability benchmark for 85% of families, Federal Reserve reports
cards.teaser: The Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta reports that 85.4% of Florida families spend more than the federal affordability benchmark on childcare, with median costs reaching nearly 17% of household income.
cards.body:
The cost of childcare in Florida far exceeds the affordability benchmark established by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, according to a report from the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta. The study found that 85.4% of Florida families are estimated to spend more than 7% of their income on childcare. In Florida, the median percentage of income families would need to pay for childcare is 16.8%. The estimated weekly costs for the care of infants and toddlers in Florida are $268, while preschool-aged children cost $208 per week.

From 2020 to 2024, childcare prices increased by 29%, compared with a 22% rise in overall prices, according to the Federal Reserve. The report said childcare costs now often "far exceed" the 7% of income affordability benchmark. The Atlanta Fed examined childcare costs in two states, Georgia and Florida. The study says the costs are putting significant financial pressure on parents and forcing difficult decisions on work hours and even leaving jobs.

cards.headline: Florida back-to-school tax holiday begins Monday, runs through August 20
cards.teaser: Florida's month-long sales tax holiday kicked off Monday, allowing families to purchase school supplies, clothing, and electronics tax-free through August 20.
cards.body:
Florida's annual back-to-school sales tax holiday kicked off Monday, giving families statewide a chance to save money on school supplies, clothing and electronics ahead of the new school year. The tax-free period runs through Thursday, August 20, allowing shoppers to purchase qualifying items without paying Florida's sales tax.

The tax holiday covers clothing, footwear, and accessories priced at $100 or less per item, including shirts, pants, dresses, shoes, boots, and accessories like belts and hats. School supplies under $50 per item are also tax-free, covering notebooks, pencils, binders, markers, scissors, and lunch boxes. Learning aids and jigsaw puzzles priced at $30 or less are included, such as flashcards, educational toys, and puzzle books. Personal computers and related accessories under $1,500 qualify for the tax exemption, including laptops, tablets, desktops, electronic book readers, and accessories like keyboards, mice, monitors, and routers. Cell phones, video game consoles, and recreational devices do not qualify. Wallets and bags under $100 per item are also covered, including backpacks, handbags, and fanny packs, though briefcases and suitcases are excluded. Governor Ron DeSantis signed the tax holiday into law as part of the state's effort to help families manage back-to-school expenses.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth backs low-altitude Blue Angels flyover after Pensacola beach incident draws safety scrutiny
cards.teaser: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth defended a Blue Angels jet that flew so low over a crowded Pensacola beach Wednesday that chairs and tents went flying, as the Pentagon dismissed another safety review.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is sticking to encouraging low-altitude military flyovers after a Navy Blue Angels jet flew extremely low over a crowded Pensacola beach on Wednesday, raising new scrutiny after the Pentagon has dismissed a series of safety reviews of such flights. Video spreading widely on social media shows the jet flying so low that chairs and tents went flying, sand kicked up, and children held their hands over their ears. The U.S. Navy said in a statement shortly afterward that it was conducting a thorough safety review. However, on Thursday morning, Trump administration officials heaped praise on the maneuver. Hegseth wrote on his personal X account that the flyovers will continue until morale improves. The Pentagon's top spokesman, Sean Parnell, wrote "Carry on Patriots" on social media alongside a photo showing a Blue Angels jet with a wingtip just feet above the heads of beachgoers. The White House tweeted a cartoon showing people on a beach taking photos of a Blue Angels jet.

Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao, a Trump administration political appointee, said the Navy had no problem with the flight and there would be no reprimands or firings. Navy officials would not say if a flight debrief was the thorough safety review the Navy said it would conduct the day prior. This marks at least the third time that Hegseth and others have voiced support for military aviators performing maneuvers that have drawn public scrutiny and military investigations. In two prior cases, Hegseth's remarks led to the end of the safety investigations. Aviation safety consultant Jeff Guzzetti, who investigated crashes for the National Transportation Safety Board and the Federal Aviation Administration, said it is shocking that the top leaders of the military would excuse this type of reckless behavior. A cavalier attitude like that can only lead to accidents in his view.

cards.headline: DEA chief joins Orlando fentanyl summit as teens, grieving parents unite against deadly drug crisis
cards.teaser: The Fentanyl Free America Summit in Orlando drew students from anti-drug coalitions nationwide, grieving parents, and DEA Administrator Terrance Cole for a coordinated response to the ongoing fentanyl threat.
cards.body:
Teens from anti-drug coalitions across the country joined grieving parents and federal law enforcement at the Fentanyl Free America Summit in Orlando this week. Hannah Kahn, 18, explained that a relative addicted to methamphetamine encouraged her to prevent addiction in others. The students came with questions and answers about how fentanyl spreads. Kahn said people often do not recognize the danger because fentanyl is frequently laced within other drugs rather than being sought out directly. Jasmine Figueroa, 19, offered pointed advice for adults on talking to young people about drugs, saying it is not a taboo topic and parents should tell children the truth about cocaine and other substances before they get educated elsewhere. Figueroa also said Narcan should be thought of as a household product like Benadryl, not just for responders and EMS.

The summit welcomed the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration as a partner this year. DEA Administrator Terrance Cole spent time with victim families and said the poison is being manufactured and distributed out of Mexico by the Mexican cartels. Cole pointed to new tools from the current administration, noting the president has designated Mexican cartels as foreign terrorists, which opens different avenues for targeting. Mari Rodriguez's daughter Imam died of fentanyl poisoning in 2023 after buying a Percocet pill laced with fentanyl. Rodriguez said the fight should have started in 2009 when the first fentanyl was found on streets.

cards.headline: Byron Donalds, David Jolly hold leads as Florida governor's race enters final primary stretch
cards.teaser: Republican U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds and Democrat David Jolly are positioned as frontrunners heading into Florida's August 18 primary, as opponents scramble for late breakthroughs.
cards.body:
Republican U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds continues to hold a commanding advantage in polling and fundraising as Florida's gubernatorial primary approaches, while Democrat David Jolly has consolidated support in the Democratic contest. A Tyson Group survey released this week placed Donalds at 48%, followed by Lt. Jay Collins at 9%, businessman James Fishback at 8%, and former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner at 4%. About 26% of respondents remained undecided. Donalds holds a major financial advantage, with his campaign announcing more than $90 million raised across his campaign operation. President Donald Trump has endorsed Donalds, while Governor Ron DeSantis has remained publicly neutral in the primary. Collins used a Thursday campaign call to position himself as the strongest Republican alternative to Donalds, arguing this is a two-person race between himself and the congressman.

Fishback is facing a $400,000 campaign from The Front Line, a Republican group aligned with U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz, over statements the group characterizes as antisemitic. His eligibility to remain in the race is also headed to court, with a two-day hearing scheduled to begin July 21 in Tallahassee. On the Democratic side, Jolly moved this week to address his past business and political relationship with Clearwater financier Leo Govoni, who federal prosecutors allege stole more than $100 million from a nonprofit. Jolly is not a defendant in the case and said he had no knowledge of the alleged theft. Florida's voter-registration deadline is July 20, with early voting offered from August 15 and the primary set for August 18.

cards.headline: Security First Insurance lowers Florida homeowners rates by average of 5.6%, launches disappearing deductible program
cards.teaser: The Ormond Beach-based insurer announced rate reductions and a new program that rewards claims-free customers by reducing their deductible 20% each year over five years.
cards.body:
Security First Insurance is lowering homeowners insurance rates by an average of 5.6%, the latest in a series of rate decreases the Florida-based company has made over the last two years. Melissa Burt DeVriese, president of Security First, said their customers are seeing the impact of the rate decreases. Insurance companies have been reducing rates or holding them stable as more companies cite a reduction in lawsuits from state reforms. Burt DeVriese said all those savings they're required to pass along to customers, and they have been.

Security First also announced new discounts and a disappearing deductible that rewards claims-free customers by reducing their deductible over time. Over the course of five years, every year the deductible goes down 20 percent as long as customers don't have a loss. Once customers have a loss, the discounted deductible applies, and then it resets back to the full deductible amount. Based in Ormond Beach, Security First has about 155,000 policies in the state. Burt DeVriese said Security First is committed to writing more policies in southeast Florida. Online firm Insurify reports that in 2026 Florida homeowners pay the highest average premium in the country at $8,292.

hero.headline: Stuart woman arrested after deputies rescue 80 cats from home in worst hoarding case Martin County sheriff has seen
hero.body:
Martin County deputies rescued dozens of cats Monday from a Stuart home that Sheriff John Budensiek described as the worst animal hoarding case he has seen in the county. The Martin County Sheriff's Office, Animal Control and Martin County Fire Rescue responded to a home in the 11500 block of Southwest Meadowlark Circle after an investigation into reports that a U.S. Postal Service employee had been collecting feral cats along her mail route.

Budensiek identified the homeowner as 77-year-old Gail Giustino. Investigators believe she was not stealing pets but was gathering feral cats and bringing them home. Authorities obtained a search warrant after Giustino allegedly refused to allow Animal Control officers inside the home during multiple attempts over the past week. When deputies entered the house Monday, they found what the sheriff described as horrific living conditions. The home had no working air conditioning, little to no ventilation and, in some areas, up to a foot of animal feces covering the floor. Budensiek said the odor was overwhelming, and Martin County Fire Rescue's Hazardous Materials Team had to ventilate the home before rescuers could safely enter.

Giustino told deputies she believed there were at least 70 cats inside the home, all kept in cages. Authorities believe there could ultimately be 70 to 80 animals or more, including several dogs, though an exact count had not been completed Monday evening. The rescued animals are being taken to the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast, which is expected to rely on foster families and volunteers to help care for them. Authorities said they are still evaluating the animals' medical conditions.

Budensiek said Giustino was arrested on two misdemeanor animal cruelty-related charges, though investigators said they could have pursued significantly more charges. The sheriff said the criminal charges were filed primarily to obtain the search warrant, remove the animals from the home and prevent Giustino from acquiring additional animals while she seeks help through the mental health court system. Budensiek said investigators believe Giustino had good intentions despite the outcome. Officials said Animal Control had previously cited Giustino dozens of times for animal-related violations about 10 years ago, but they believe she gradually returned to hoarding animals after complying with earlier code enforcement requirements.

cards.headline: Murray Middle School demolition begins after Hurricane Milton tornado damage
cards.teaser: Murray Middle School demolition is underway in Martin County, marking the start of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage caused by Hurricane Milton.
cards.body:
Murray Middle School demolition is underway in Martin County, marking the start of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage caused by Hurricane Milton. The project includes reconstruction of buildings destroyed in the tornadoes, along with a new administration building, media center, art lab, and a full overhaul of the parking lot. The demolition phase alone costs $3.3 million, though the total project cost has not been finalized. The project is being funded by local capital improvement, sales tax and Public Education Capital Outlay. Students who were displaced from the affected classrooms will continue learning in portable classrooms until construction is complete.

Kirstie Gernaine, coordinator of public information and community relations for the Martin County School District, said Murray Middle School was already slated to get all of this construction work with a new admin area, a new media center and a brand new art lab. With Hurricane Milton and those tornadoes destroying the buildings in the back buildings 18, 10, and nine, the district was able to add these on. The school district said parents can be assured their students will be safe during construction. Barriers have already been placed around the work zone to keep students out. The district hopes to complete the renovations by December 2027.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County man leads Martin County deputies on high-speed chase through Indiantown
cards.teaser: A Palm Beach County man led Martin County deputies on a high-speed chase through Indiantown after driving more than 100 mph on State Road 710.
cards.body:
Deputies spotted 33-year-old Markell Tillman driving aggressively at speeds exceeding 100 mph on State Road 710, forcing other vehicles off the roadway. When deputies attempted to stop him, Tillman fled. He weaved through traffic in an attempt to lose deputies before turning onto SW Martin Highway toward Palm City, where he continued to drive recklessly. Deputies spotted Tillman again traveling eastbound on Martin Highway near Allapattah Road. Deputies used stop sticks to disable his vehicle near I-95.

Tillman then bailed out of the vehicle and attempted to flee on foot before deputies caught up with him and took him into custody. He was arrested on fleeing and eluding, aggravated fleeing with injury or damage, operating a vehicle exceeding the speed limit by 50 or more mph, driving while license suspended or revoked, obstruction without violence, and operating a vehicle at 100 or more mph. Tillman also had an out-of-county warrant at the time of his arrest. He was booked into the Martin County Jail.

cards.headline: Safe Kids Treasure Coast providing free pool alarms to Martin County residents
cards.teaser: The Florida Department of Health and Safe Kids Treasure Coast are providing a limited supply of free pool alarms to qualifying residents in Martin County.
cards.body: The Florida Department of Health and Safe Kids Treasure Coast are providing a limited supply of free pool alarms to qualifying residents in Martin County. A pool alarm is one layer of protection and should always be used alongside close adult supervision, pool barriers and water safety education to help prevent drowning, the coalition said. Safe Kids Treasure Coast is asking residents to fill out a survey to determine eligibility. The program is available to Martin County residents with a residential pool, with one alarm per household. There are no income or priority group requirements. Available while supplies last. A 9-volt battery is required to operate the alarm but is not included. For more information, residents can call 772-462-3501.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound couple seeks support as husband battles head and neck cancer
cards.teaser: A Hobe Sound couple is asking for community support as they navigate a cancer diagnosis, holding onto faith every step of the way.
cards.body:
Dave and Faren Motz met in South Florida before moving to Maui, where they married and raised their family. Faren said she raised all three of their kids and home schooled them, and the couple started a business with a farm where they served children. Years later, the couple moved to Hobe Sound and purchased a property, but just months after settling in, Dave was diagnosed with head and neck cancer. As the couple searched for the right healthcare in Florida, AdventHealth in Celebration provided programs and grants that became a critical resource.

Dave underwent nearly seven weeks of daily radiation treatments. The repeated visits to Orlando, biopsies, scans, and exams added up, costing the couple nearly $20,000 out of pocket. Their age and income kept them from qualifying for Medicare or Medicaid. Doctors told Dave he has an 85% chance of recovery. Dave, a former firefighter, had long been the family's provider, and now Faren has stepped up to support them both. Faren works at Latitudes at the Jupiter Beach Resort, where those who want to show their support can stop by and visit. Those who would like to contribute financially can donate to the family's GoFundMe at Standing with Dave Motz in his cancer battle.

cards.headline: More Than 70 Animals Found in Stuart Home During Large-Scale Hoarding Response
cards.teaser: More than 70 animals were believed to be living inside a sweltering and heavily contaminated Stuart home where Martin County authorities carried out a search warrant Monday, accord
cards.body:
More than 70 animals were believed to be living inside a sweltering and heavily contaminated Stuart home where Martin County authorities carried out a search warrant Monday, according to Sheriff John Budensiek.

Budensiek said the number of animals could ultimately reach 80 or more as deputies, Animal Services officers, Martin County Fire Rescue personnel and the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast continued working at the property.

The investigation began several weeks ago after a U.S. Postal Service employee reported that a woman appeared to be collecting or taking cats while traveling along her route, Budensiek said.

Investigators determined that the 77-year-old resident had a previous history with Martin County Animal Services. Budensiek said authorities had responded to animal-related concerns at the property approximately a decade earlier, issuing dozens of citations and helping the resident address problems involving ventilation and the care of the animals.

Animal Services officers returned to the home last week to determine whether the animals were being properly housed and whether neglect or abuse was occurring. However, Budensiek said the resident would not allow officers to fully inspect the property.

Although she surrendered several animals, she continued preventing authorities from accessing the home, according to the sheriff. Investigators subsequently obtained a search warrant and returned Monday.

Budensiek said the odor coming from the home could be detected from outside. Once responders entered, they encountered extreme heat, poor ventilation, animal waste and no functioning air conditioning.

"There could be north of 70 or 80 animals," Budensiek said during the briefing, describing areas of the home as being covered with animal feces.

The conditions were so severe that responders used protective equipment while entering and removing animals from the property. Budensiek described the interior as stifling and said crews worked to ventilate the home while attempting to safely locate and recover the animals.

Despite the conditions, Budensiek emphasized that investigators did not believe the resident was deliberately trying to harm the animals.

He said that if authorities viewed her as an intentional animal abuser, she would have been taken to jail. Instead, the sheriff characterized the situation as an animal-hoarding case involving a woman who had become overwhelmed and also needed assistance.

Budensiek said the immediate priorities were saving the animals, providing any medical treatment they require and connecting the resident with appropriate help.

The large number of animals created a significant logistical challenge for the agencies at the scene. The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast was expected to receive animals initially, but additional assistance from volunteers, rescue organizations, foster homes and potential adopters could be needed.

Each animal must also be documented and evaluated before authorities can determine its condition and appropriate placement.

Budensiek said the final number of animals remained uncertain while the operation continued. Authorities were also working through legal questions involving ownership and whether the resident would voluntarily surrender the animals.

No arrest was announced during the sheriff's briefing. Any potential citations or other legal action will depend on the results of the investigation and the conditions documented inside the home.

The response was expected to continue as crews worked through the property and arranged shelter and care for the animals.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County residents adjust diets as E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks spread
cards.teaser: Health officials confirmed five local cases of cyclospora since May, including two in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County, prompting residents to change what they eat and avoid.
cards.body:
Concerns over contaminated produce linked to E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks are prompting South Florida residents to reconsider their food choices, with some avoiding leafy greens entirely. The outbreaks have affected thousands nationwide and include lettuce connected to Taco Bell locations. Health officials have confirmed local cases stretching from the Palm Beaches to the Treasure Coast, including two cases in St. Lucie County.

 The Florida Department of Health reported five confirmed local cases of cyclospora since May. Two cases were reported in Palm Beach County, two in St. Lucie County, and one in Martin County. The contamination concerns have led families across the region to change their eating habits at restaurants, grocery stores, and fast-food chains.

 Dakota and Brynlee Rhodes, who were visiting Delray Beach with their mother Jenny, said they are trying to stay away from lettuce and stuff like that. Other families are similarly steering clear of leafy greens altogether as reports of contaminated produce continue to spread across the country. The widespread nature of the outbreaks has left many consumers uncertain about which products are safe to purchase and consume.

 Samantha Barone, a dietitian for the bariatric program at Delray Medical Center, offered guidance for consumers looking to maintain healthy diets while avoiding potentially contaminated produce. Barone recommends sticking to melon and things that have a harder skin that you can peel. She advises consumers to focus on produce with protective outer layers and to wash all fruits and vegetables thoroughly before eating them.

 For those seeking alternatives to leafy greens, Barone suggests that beans and nuts are safe options that still provide fiber and protein. She specifically recommends cleaning produce using a mixture of one part distilled white vinegar to three parts water. The outbreaks have highlighted the importance of proper food handling and preparation practices for consumers across South Florida.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County Fire District terminates 3 firefighters after hazing investigation
hero.teaser: St. Lucie County Fire District released investigative reports detailing allegations of hazing and workplace misconduct that led to the termination of 3 firefighters and the suspension of 2 others.
hero.body:
St. Lucie County Fire District administrators first received videos in March 2026 showing what they described as senior firefighters using a modified bug zapper to administer electric shocks to probationary and apprentice firefighters while on duty. The district said the incidents occurred during shifts in March and September 2024. The videos prompted Fire Chief Jeff Lee to hire an outside attorney to conduct an independent investigation rather than handle the matter internally. Attorney J.K. Keller, of Allen, Norton & Blue, concluded that a preponderance of the evidence showed probationary employees had been subjected to hazing by senior firefighters and supervisors. Keller also determined the conduct violated multiple district policies, including workplace violence and employee conduct rules.

The investigative report describes videos showing probationary firefighters being questioned while connected to the modified device and receiving electrical shocks when they answered incorrectly. Other videos allegedly show probationary firefighters voluntarily allowing themselves to be shocked while coworkers looked on. Investigators concluded that any claimed consent was undermined by the power imbalance between senior firefighters and probationary employees. The district said it followed Keller's recommendations by terminating 3 employees and issuing 48-hour unpaid suspensions to 2 others. The disciplined employees have exercised their contractual rights to challenge the actions through the grievance and arbitration process.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office makes 2nd arrest in fatal shooting of Fort Pierce art teacher
cards.teaser: Dale A. Mincey, 41, nephew of victim Andre Leonard Barnes, was formally charged with first-degree murder Saturday in connection with the art teacher's death.
cards.body:
Dale A. Mincey, 41, was formally charged with first-degree murder Saturday in connection with the death of his uncle, Andre Leonard Barnes, 66. Mincey remains in custody at the St. Lucie County Jail and is being held without bond. The fatal shooting happened July 7 at a residence on the 2700 block of Essex Drive. Deputies responded to the home at around 3:30 p.m. after receiving reports of a person with a gunshot wound. When deputies arrived, they learned a man had shot another man with a rifle. Barnes was taken to a local hospital, where he died. During questioning, Mincey told detectives he could not recall what happened the day of the shooting and that he didn't have any issues with Barnes and did not know how Barnes died, an arrest affidavit said. However, he admitted to owning two firearms.

Karen Moye, Barnes' sister and Mincey's mother, was also at the home when the shooting occurred. She heard a loud bang while she was in the bathroom and came out to find Mincey and called police, an arrest affidavit said. Moye is also facing charges in this fatal shooting, which deputies said was premeditated. Sheriff Richard Del Toro said Tuesday during a press conference that Moye knowingly provided false information to investigators and withheld pertinent information related to the homicide investigation. She has been charged with false report to law enforcement and the commission of a capital felony. Barnes worked as an art teacher for the St. Lucie County School District since 2017, serving at West Gate K-8 and Samuel S. Gaines Academy. Barnes leaves behind three adult children.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Sheriff ramps up traffic enforcement with focus on speeding, reckless driving
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office is intensifying traffic enforcement this summer, deploying additional deputies and launching a new targeting initiative aimed at reducing speeding and reckless driving across the county.
cards.body:
Sheriff Richard Del Toro said traffic is the top concern among residents and described the crackdown as a quality of life issue. Del Toro is using extra deputies from the sheriff's school resource division to boost enforcement while the school year is on break. He is also placing top-performing deputies in areas of concern. Deputies Christopher Rodrigues and Cheyenne Benning are among those targeting high-problem corridors, including Midway Road, U.S. Highway 1 and Indian River Drive.

Benning said she most recently had someone pass her on I-95 doing 105 mph. Rodrigues said he got a girl doing 72 mph on Midway Road and clocked someone at 98 mph on U.S. Highway 1. On Indian River Drive, which has a 25 mph speed limit, his top speed was 73 mph. In the past four weeks, deputies conducted 1,162 traffic stops, wrote 470 citations and issued 1,728 written warnings. The enforcement push is part of a broader strategy Del Toro put in place when he took office. He eliminated the agency's dedicated traffic unit and made traffic enforcement the responsibility of every deputy. Since 2025, the sheriff's office has issued more than 26,000 citations, a 155% increase.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie couple fights rezoning of lot behind their home, says voices went unheard
cards.teaser: A Port St. Lucie couple is searching for answers after the city council voted to rezone the lot behind their home from residential to commercial, despite their months-long opposition.
cards.body:
The Mucciolos have called Port St. Lucie home for years, drawn to the property by its beautiful setting and backyard views of nature. In a unanimous vote, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved changing the lot behind their yard, where trees currently stand, to be rezoned from residential to commercial. The council says the change is necessary to reduce traffic in the neighborhood. One council member said adding commercial closer to neighborhoods reduces the length of trips, which reduces overall traffic because shorter trips reduce the burden on the overall network. Joseph Mucciolo said the trees will be gone in six months or a year.

The two spoke at Monday's meeting, voicing their concerns, but they feel the council left them unheard. The council held its second reading Monday. While there was public comment, it was what's called a quasi-judicial hearing, meaning council members act as a panel of judges, applying existing zoning rules to a specific property and making decisions based strictly on sworn testimony and factual evidence, not public opinion. Joseph Mucciolo said the couple fought for months and feels their voices have gone unheard except for the news media. The Mucciolos say they will be exploring any kind of appeal process to change this outcome or to change the next one. Margaret Mucciolo said the process needs to change until it's logical, transparent, caring, and provides hope for people.

cards.headline: New tuition-free tech school SouthTech Treasure Coast to open in Fort Pierce in August
cards.teaser: A new tuition-free career and technical charter school is preparing to open in Fort Pierce in August, bringing a hands-on approach to education to the Treasure Coast.
cards.body:
SouthTech Treasure Coast will give middle and high school students the opportunity to earn industry certifications while completing their traditional coursework, helping them build real-world skills and prepare for high-demand careers before they graduate. The St. Lucie County School Board approved the charter application for the Fort Pierce campus in April. School leaders say they selected the Treasure Coast because of the area's growing demand for skilled workers. Nicole Handy, Director of Expansion of SouthTech Schools, said the school is targeting high paying careers that are growing and expanding in the Fort Pierce area.

The Fort Pierce campus will serve students in grades 6 through 12, with plans to enroll about 460 students in its first year. Students will have the opportunity to choose from career academies including medical science, culinary arts, cosmetology, and agriculture technology. SouthTech Treasure Coast will host a grand opening celebration on Saturday, July 25, from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m., giving families and community members a chance to tour the new campus and learn more about the programs being offered. SouthTech Treasure Coast in Fort Pierce is located at 2810 S. US Highway 1 Fort Pierce, FL 34982.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County residents adjust diets as E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks spread
cards.teaser: Health officials confirmed five local cases of cyclospora since May, including two in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County, prompting residents to change what they eat and avoid.
cards.body:
Concerns over contaminated produce linked to E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks are prompting South Florida residents to reconsider their food choices, with some avoiding leafy greens entirely. The outbreaks have affected thousands nationwide and include lettuce connected to Taco Bell locations. Health officials have confirmed local cases stretching from the Palm Beaches to the Treasure Coast, including two cases in St. Lucie County.

 The Florida Department of Health reported five confirmed local cases of cyclospora since May. Two cases were reported in Palm Beach County, two in St. Lucie County, and one in Martin County. The contamination concerns have led families across the region to change their eating habits at restaurants, grocery stores, and fast-food chains.

 Dakota and Brynlee Rhodes, who were visiting Delray Beach with their mother Jenny, said they are trying to stay away from lettuce and stuff like that. Other families are similarly steering clear of leafy greens altogether as reports of contaminated produce continue to spread across the country. The widespread nature of the outbreaks has left many consumers uncertain about which products are safe to purchase and consume.

 Samantha Barone, a dietitian for the bariatric program at Delray Medical Center, offered guidance for consumers looking to maintain healthy diets while avoiding potentially contaminated produce. Barone recommends sticking to melon and things that have a harder skin that you can peel. She advises consumers to focus on produce with protective outer layers and to wash all fruits and vegetables thoroughly before eating them.

 For those seeking alternatives to leafy greens, Barone suggests that beans and nuts are safe options that still provide fiber and protein. She specifically recommends cleaning produce using a mixture of one part distilled white vinegar to three parts water. The outbreaks have highlighted the importance of proper food handling and preparation practices for consumers across South Florida.

hero.headline: Fellsmere animal sanctuary rebuilds with $100,000 after fire killed 11 cats
hero.body:
A Fellsmere animal sanctuary is rebuilding with community support after a devastating fire on March 9 destroyed the facility and killed 11 cats. For the Love of Paws, founded by Ted Pankiewicz in 2014 as a memorial to his late wife, has received more than $100,000 in donations to help reconstruct the sanctuary. Pankiewicz suffered burns to his arms while trying to save animals during the fire. His wife had always dreamed of starting a rescue operation, and he turned that vision into reality after her passing.

The sanctuary operates as a permanent home for animals rather than a traditional rescue facility. When pets arrive at For the Love of Paws, they stay for the remainder of their lives and are cared for as if they were Pankiewicz's own animals. Beyond providing shelter, the organization serves vulnerable community members by distributing 12,000 to 15,000 pounds of pet food monthly to senior citizens, disabled individuals, and veterans who struggle to feed their pets. This community service has made the sanctuary an important resource for the Treasure Coast's most vulnerable residents and their animal companions.

The rebuilt facility will incorporate extensive safety features to prevent another tragedy. The new building will be constructed entirely of steel, a significant upgrade from the previous structure. Pankiewicz plans to install a security system with smoke detectors that will immediately alert the fire department when triggered, eliminating any delay in emergency response. An interior sprinkler system will also be installed throughout the building. Pankiewicz acknowledged the cats might not appreciate the sprinklers, joking that the system will likely annoy them, but added that it would be better than the alternative. The new sanctuary will maintain its cage-free philosophy, with plans for an outdoor catio where cats can roam freely in a protected environment.

The community response to the tragedy moved Pankiewicz deeply. He described the outpouring of support as equally emotional as the fire itself, but in an opposite way. "The fire made us cry tears of sorrow, and the community made us cry tears of gratitude," Pankiewicz said. The substantial fundraising effort demonstrates the community's recognition of the sanctuary's importance to both the animals it shelters and the people it serves. The new steel structure with enhanced safety systems will ensure that For the Love of Paws can continue its mission of providing permanent homes for animals and supporting pet owners in need.

cards.teaser: JetBlue is ending its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on September 9. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched in December.
cards.body:
Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said the decision reflects how the airline industry operates. Dambeck said JetBlue was not seeing the ridership numbers it had hoped for on the JFK route. The route launched last December. cards.headline: Indian River County families can apply for free or reduced-price school meals starting July 15
cards.teaser: Families in Indian River County are able to apply for free or reduced price meals for students starting July 15. Students at six Indian River County schools can receive free meals during the 2026-2027 school year through federal nutrition programs.
cards.body:
Families in Indian River County can apply for free or reduced-price meals for students starting July 15. Students at six Indian River County schools can receive free meals during the 2026-2027 school year through federal nutrition programs. Other families in the district may still qualify for free or reduced-price meals based on household size and income criteria. Families are encouraged to complete one application per household to determine eligibility.

To apply, families need their child's Student ID number, their child's full formal name as listed in FOCUS, a valid email address, and internet access or the LINQ Connect mobile app. Families receiving Florida Medicaid benefits should have their 10-digit Medicaid case number that begins with the number 1. To complete the application, families visit www.LINQConnect.com, sign in or create an account, search for Indian River County Public Schools in Vero Beach, and add their student by entering the Student ID and formal name as listed in FOCUS. From the website homepage, families click School Services at the top menu and then select Free and Reduced Meal Application. The application requires household information and income details. Families with questions about the meal programs can contact Shawn O'Keefe, the district's nutrition services director, at 772-564-5041 or shawn.okeefe@indianriverschools.org.

cards.headline: JetBlue ending Vero Beach to New York JFK route in September due to low demand
cards.teaser: JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as th
cards.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating in September. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast. Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said the decision reflects how the airline industry operates based on passenger numbers.

 "It's just the way that that market works, and air carriers will fluctuate based off of demand," Dambeck said. He added that JetBlue "just wasn't seeing what they were hoping for" with the New York route.

 Not everyone agrees the route had a fair shot at success. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time if given more opportunity. "I think if they hung in there, it would have worked.

 I think it would have built up pretty good," Ahern said. He noted the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach, saying, "It's easy. It's close." His comments reflect concerns from local travelers who appreciated having direct access to New York without driving to larger airports in South Florida or Orlando.

 The Boston route continues to perform well at Vero Beach Regional Airport, with Dambeck saying "Boston is seeing great demand." Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time, demonstrating continued interest in that northeastern connection. The contrast between the two routes highlights how different markets can perform differently even when serving similar geographic regions. While both Boston and New York are major northeastern cities, the Boston service has attracted enough passengers to remain viable while the JFK route struggled to build a sustainable customer base.

 Dambeck said the door is not closed on the JFK route returning in the future, noting "They'll evaluate continuously. So just because it's gone now doesn't mean that it never will come back." This leaves open the possibility that JetBlue could restore service to New York if conditions change or demand increases. Airlines regularly reassess their route networks based on seasonal patterns, economic conditions, and shifting travel preferences. For now, Vero Beach travelers seeking to reach New York will need to connect through other cities or use alternative airports.
